clue.text: Sample of fine writing father's left in plant

indicators.note: left means gone away, so these letters depart from the longer phrase

parts.note: a purple passage is a showy, ornate piece of prose
father is PA, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone finds an elegant written extract their father has abandoned inside a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes PAS (PA plus the S of 's) out of PURPLE PASSAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple-flowered sagebrush of the American West, famous from Zane Grey's novel title, is a shrub.

clue.text: Tiresome figure seen in part of window, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a single sheet of glass in a window frame

explanation.surface: A dull shape glimpsed through a section of a window, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an annoying, wearisome person is called a nuisance or a pain in everyday speech.

clue.text: Revolutionary artist left caustic material for retrospective

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: retrospective means looking backwards, so the following letters run in reverse order

parts.note: acid is a corrosive, caustic substance

explanation.surface: An artist abandons corrosive substances in favour of mounting a retrospective exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' reads like an art show, but here it signals backwards reading; RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a revolutionary person or idea favours sweeping, root-and-branch change.

clue.text: Partridge, say, girl, ex-poacher, shot

definitions.note: Eric Partridge compiled famous dictionaries of slang

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl, once a poacher, shoots a partridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partridge' looks like the game bird in a poaching scene, but it is Eric Partridge, the dictionary-maker; 'shot' is the anagram signal on GIRL EXPOACHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Eric Partridge was a celebrated compiler of dictionaries of slang and usage.

clue.text: Like one in Home Counties close to station getting wet

indicators.note: in places the first piece within the second here

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, SE
one is an odd number, so like one means odd

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word station, its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone from the commuter belt round London gets drenched near the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, abbreviated SE for south-east; ODD goes inside, then N, the last letter of 'station'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked through: something drenched and saturated has been getting thoroughly wet.

clue.text: Decline game with doubles team, we hear, and top tennis player

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: a doubles pairing has two players
a seed is a ranked player placed in a tournament draw

explanation.surface: A tennis scene: a game with a doubles pair and a leading player.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for deteriorating: a plant that runs to seed, like a person, declines past its best.

clue.text: Nothing is to be removed from a model part of church

indicators.note: removed from tells us to take the first piece out of what follows

parts.note: to model is to pose
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An instruction that nothing should be taken away from a scale model of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Silly posh royalty occupying stately home

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so these letters go within the house

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing house
U means upper-class, posh
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Foolish upper-class royals moving into a grand country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: childish and foolish behaviour is silly.

clue.text: Enthusiasm? It's right in upcoming sporting establishment in middle of week to show it

indicators.note: in places the whole assembly inside those central letters
middle of takes the central letters of the word week
in puts the legal right inside the reversed club
upcoming in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a club, such as a golf or tennis club
a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Enthusiasm should be shown properly at a club in midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is the legal sense: a lien, a right to retain property. 'upcoming' reverses the club because this is a down clue. 'It's' and 'to show it' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bubbling exuberance and zest are both forms of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Independent? Old edition is put in list

parts.note: ex means former, old

explanation.surface: A query about whether an independent publication's back issue has been catalogued.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalogued: an item entered in an index has been listed.

clue.text: Greek character carrying accomplished picture

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the Greek letter holds the other word inside it

parts.note: tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet
able means skilled, accomplished

explanation.surface: A Greek person bearing a skilful painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene or arrangement, as in a painting or posed group of actors.

clue.text: Executives favoured doctor with cultured disposition for those before passage?

parts.note: a company's board of directors
in means fashionable, in favour
a GP is a general practitioner
arty means having artistic pretensions

explanation.surface: Directors preferred a doctor with refined tastes for some purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: people who board a ship are those embarking before a sea voyage, or 'passage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A group going aboard a vessel, before or during its passage, often to seize or inspect it.

clue.text: Mutt cancels poker I fancy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imaginative, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A card player calls off a poker game on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like a verb meaning I'd like, but it signals the anagram of CANCELS POKER I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutt is a dog, especially a mongrel; this gundog breed is an example.

clue.text: Prince on holiday in unsatisfactory place for the great and good

definitions.text: place for the great and good

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

indicators.note: in puts the time-away word inside the poor one

parts.note: a lame excuse is unsatisfactory
off means away from work

explanation.surface: A royal on vacation ends up somewhere disappointing, where notables gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery or institution honouring the most celebrated people in a field.

clue.text: Maintain a part of mountain for radio coverage

indicators.note: on radio only the sound is heard, so the phrase is taken as spoken

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf on a rock face, with a

explanation.surface: Insisting that a section of a mountain is wanted for broadcasting signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to assert or claim something, often without proof.

clue.text: Attentiveness shown by aspiring teacher around academy and second person doubly so

indicators.note: around means the degree letters encircle the single letter

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is the degree of a would-be teacher

indicators.note: doubly so means the pronoun appears twice

parts.note: ye is the old second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A trainee teacher at an academy and a colleague are both showing great attentiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, watchful observation: a gaze that misses nothing is close attentiveness.

clue.text: Flower old woman found around island with extended area to the north

indicators.note: around means the mother word encloses the rest

parts.note: ma is mother, an old woman

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: long means extended

explanation.surface: A mother found a flower on an island with a large northern expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flowering tree or shrub with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Member of pack given a means to hide

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in a rugby scrum, the pack
a way is a method or means

explanation.surface: A rugby forward is given a way to conceal something.
explanation.walkthrough: The pack is the forwards of a rugby team; the lock is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to secure something out of sight, keeping it hidden.

clue.text: Smoothie, drink the writer put in posh car

parts.note: cha is tea

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the car letters

parts.note: RR is Rolls-Royce
the writer refers to the setter, ME

explanation.surface: A smoothie drinker places the writer in a luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoothie' looks like a drink beside 'drink', but it means a smooth-talking person.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is a suave, ingratiating person, someone who wins people over with charm.

clue.text: Note pounds pocketed by retrograde peer in wholesale fashion

indicators.note: pocketed by means held inside the following letters
retrograde means moving backwards, so the name runs in reverse

parts.note: Lord Coe, the athlete Sebastian Coe, is a peer
NB, nota bene, means note well
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Money is quietly taken by a backward-looking member of the Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrograde' turns COE into EOC, which holds NB and L.
explanation.definitionFit: French phrase meaning all together, as a whole, which is wholesale.

clue.text: Principally, naughty joke in office from the distant past

indicators.note: in means the joke letters go inside the toilet

parts.note: the offices is an old euphemism for the lavatory, the loo

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, so take the first letter of naughty

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A smutty joke mainly told at the workplace, dating from years back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' looks like a workplace, but it is an old British euphemism for the lavatory (LOO).
explanation.definitionFit: Adverbial phrase: at a time far back in history, in the remote past.

clue.text: Son getting premier case for weapon

parts.note: Edward Heath was UK Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A son becomes Prime Minister and needs a holster.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was the British Prime Minister in the early 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting cover for a sword or dagger blade.

clue.text: Panic about sport largely linked to explosive article? It has short-lived impact

indicators.note: about means the panic letters go round the next pieces

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the last letter drops off

parts.note: shinty is a Scottish game like hockey
HE is high explosive
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Alarm over a sport tied to a bomb, which makes only a brief stir.
explanation.walkthrough: SHINTY, a Scottish stick game, loses its Y to 'largely'; with HE it goes 'about'-ed by FLAP. The surface's flintlock 'explosive article' hints at the phrase's origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from a flintlock musket's priming powder flaring without firing: a sudden success that quickly fades.

clue.text: Burning material hoarded by grumpy retiree

indicators.note: hoarded by means kept inside these words, running across them

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered pensioner stockpiling fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of combustible wood used for burning a body at a funeral.

clue.text: Part of wheel kept in car that's returning naval figure

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the whole thing reads backwards
kept in means held within the car's name

parts.note: Lada is a Russian make of car
the rim is the outer edge of a wheel

explanation.surface: A wheel part stored inside a vehicle on its way back, belonging to a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior officer commanding a fleet or navy.

clue.text: A rook that's nested in front by yard previously

indicators.note: nested in means settled inside the next word, like a bird

parts.note: to be in the lead is to be at the front
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird that built its nest in the front garden, by the yard, before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like the bird, nesting fits that, but it is R from chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something done before now or before then has been done previously.

clue.text: Title is precious thing having been stripped of power

indicators.note: stripped of means the letter is taken away

parts.note: a pearl is a precious gem

explanation.surface: A title is a treasure even after its authority has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman's rank: a British peerage title ranking above a viscount.

clue.text: Last of dull chores may after shift make one tearful

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word dull
shift means move around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The tail end of tedious housework may, after a work shift, leave someone in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work period, but it rearranges L (end of 'dull') and CHORES MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: weepy, given to shedding tears.
